name: Lynx
summary: The classic text-based web browser — navigate the web from your terminal
description:
Lynx is the world's oldest actively maintained web browser. It renders web pages as plain text in your terminal, making it perfect for:

• Browsing the web on headless servers or over SSH
• Fast, distraction-free reading without JavaScript, CSS, or ads
• Accessibility — works with screen readers and braille displays
• Low-bandwidth connections and ancient hardware
• Scripting and automation of web tasks

Lynx supports HTTPS, cookies, authentication, and HTML forms. It doesn't support JavaScript, CSS, or modern web apps — but for text-heavy sites (Wikipedia, documentation, news, forums) it's often faster and cleaner than any graphical browser.

KEYSTROKES
• G or g — Go to URL
• ↓/↑ or Tab/Shift+Tab — Navigate links
• → or Enter — Follow link
• ← or Backspace — Go back
• H — Help screen
• Q — Quit
• / — Search within page
• = — Page info (URL, size, etc.)
• ! — Shell escape
• Ctrl+R — Reload

INSTALLATION
Available in the official Arch repositories. Just run the install command below and press Enter — no password needed for the store package.
